summary: A steel fire tower in Indiana's Clark State Forest, built around 1927-1930; standing but closed for improvements, with its stairs restricted.

facts.design: Steel fire tower with a cab; an earlier wooden tower stood about one mile northeast in the late 1920s

access.note: Indiana DNR notice says the tower is closed for improvements, which restricts use of the stairs, and that it will reopen once the work is finished. Indiana Fire Towers reports it was under repair and closed to climbing in 2023 and 2024.

visit.trail_note: Inside Clark State Forest near Henryville, Indiana. The DNR notice gives no reopening date.

facts.agency: Indiana Division of Forestry (per NHLR); Clark State Forest is listed under the Indiana Department of Natural Resources

events.note: Annual report says a telephone line is being built to Grandview Tower, to be used as a fire tower until a steel one can be erected.
Steel tower. The sign on site says constructed 1928; a 1932 state list says erected 1927; the register says built around 1930.
Kokomo Tribune item (July 19, 1930) describes an observer who, in the fall and spring, phones the warden when and where a fire starts.
Forest Service history says Indiana began building lookout towers in 1930 and that at that time it had only one fire tower, at Clark State Forest.
Under repair and closed to climbing in 2023 and 2024, per Indiana Fire Towers.
Fire in the cab on May 17, 2025, per information and pictures posted on Facebook and cited by Indiana Fire Towers. Fire department response reported.

corrections.why: No source read gives this tower's height. 12.2 m equals 40 ft; the only 40-foot figure found is a 1989 newspaper item about a fall from a 40-foot tower in the Clark State Forest, which does not name this tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says built around 1930. A 1932 state list (via Indiana Fire Towers) says erected 1927, and the sign on site says 1928. The 1928 annual report notes a new steel tower. The story gives the range rather than picking one date.

The 1927 annual report counts two fire towers on the state forest, but says one was erected by the United States Government for geodetic survey work. The Forest Service history says that when Indiana began building lookout towers in 1930 it had only one fire tower, at Clark State Forest. The story reports both statements and the geodetic detail.
The 1930 Kokomo item gives 1,080 feet for the knob; the register gives 1,035 ft (315 m), which matches the record's elevation_m of 315.5. The story does not use an elevation figure.

notes_for_editor: The DNR closure notice is undated in the cache, so the closed status is as of the last read and should be rechecked before publication. The May 2025 fire comes from Facebook posts cited by a personal enthusiast site; the story attributes it to that site. The brief's height_m of 12.2 m is not supported by any source read. Indiana Fire Towers also describes a personal climb in 2021; that is not used and is not encouraged. The 1989 accident report is not in the story because it does not name this tower. The old NHLR Lookout.aspx page returned HTTP 500 and was not used. One websearch.py search was run. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the 1927 two-tower statement is now shown with the geodetic-survey context from the same page; the observer detail keeps the fall-and-spring qualifier; the still-standing and not-climbable status is footnoted.
